key_insight: The paper shows that conventional FPV can decouple flamelet state from local strain rate, and proposes an ε-based flamelet coupling that more consistently ties combustion response to the turbulence field.
engineering_relevance: For reacting-flow simulations, the ε–Z formulation can improve physical consistency in strained mixing layers and better predict quenching, product persistence, and flamelet-state selection under high strain.
method: Performed 2D RANS simulations of a transonic accelerating reacting mixing layer.
Compared one-step kinetics, conventional FPV, and the proposed ε–Z flamelet model.
Used ε to infer imposed flamelet strain rate S* and explicitly transported selected species.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports comparative numerical results showing that FPV preferentially samples near-equilibrium flamelet states in high-strain regions, while the ε–Z model maintains a tighter link between the computed strain field and flamelet response.
watch_item: The new ε-based coupling depends on modeled turbulence quantities and tabulated chemistry assumptions, so accuracy may still be sensitive to closure quality and manifold validity outside the calibrated regime.
